title: aider-builds-a-piece
owner: CC owns the code, the proofs and the probe. Akien owns the intention (the offload thesis is his, captured verbatim 2026-08-15) and owns the disposition the watch feeds: offload-more vs pull-back is his call at triage, never the probe's.
intention: Give the aider shim a builder loop: carry ONE piece of a cast ticket from its berthed brief to an applied edit plus a run test result. It runs inside the shim's own venv interpreter (the only place aider is importable with our surfaces standing), calls translate.brief() for the prompt and file lists, calls holder.hold(), constructs aider's Coder from the brief's fields (map_tokens=0, auto_commits OFF), runs one edit pass confined to brief.files, runs the piece's test_cmd, and returns serializable data. It STAMPS THE TICKET on every recorded ask — a field fence.SeenLog.record already takes and nothing supplies. It does NOT write a verdict artifact and crosses nothing: disposing the result stays CC's act at /sail step 6.
why: The shim is complete and INERT — zero callers repo-wide outside its own folder, and translate.py says the gap in its own words: 'A brief is data; running it is someone else's.' There is no someone else, so offloading a build to the apprentice cannot happen, and therefore cannot be measured. Law 1 is the aim (the resolver spent on the novel; a mechanical piece built from a settled chart chain is the definition of not-novel) and Law 3 is the urgency (hypothesis 8 — does offloading yield? — was marked CARRIED at aider-shim's verdict and stays unmeasured until a real ticket goes through). The measured symptom: the offload probe reads shimmed:0, rows:0, and its population is empty BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by nothing-having-happened-yet — all four allowed asks in the log carry ticket:'', because the live fire drove a synthetic piece and nothing else has ever driven anything.
traces_to: Telos 1 (demonstrate inference compilation) and Telos 5 (self-improving — the system building itself with a cheaper hand). Law 1 as the operative one. Law 3 for the measurement it unblocks. Law 8 for the shape of the watch: a green earned by the supervisor rather than the apprentice is a hollow green, and hollow green is worse here than red.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam@v2 invariant: proved + feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). ENTRY at BUILDME: refuses without a berthed validate packet claiming this ticket (buildme-rides-the-chart) and without intent_berth + sorted_berth — which for this node is not ceremony, since survey is where the venv/test-runnability assumption gets measured. PROVE at PROVEME: tester runs the proofs beside the code, netns isolation, sink='validations'. EXIT at PROVED: refuses without a complete passing verdict artifact answering every criterion of the claiming validate berth by its instrument (proved-answers-the-chart). EMISSION at WATCHME: refuses unless a module declaring a frozen module-level PROBE stands at the probe berth above. KICKS BACK ON: a red proof (back-edge to BUILDME); a failed criterion at step 6 is a kick-back, not a crossing. Check-type is machine throughout — proved by running the code, never by review.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a real cast ticket's piece is carried brief -> applied edit -> run test result, with the ask recorded carrying that ticket, and the offload probe's `shimmed` count moves off 0 (measured at 0 today). WRONG-INTENT when the driven edits need rewriting by CC more often than they survive, or when supervising a driven piece costs more tool calls than building it by hand would have — either kills the offload thesis, and the driver is then the instrument that killed it rather than a failed build.
falsifier.horizon: Re-read when the first real ticket has been driven, OR on 2026-09-16 (30 days) if nothing has been driven by then. The second clause is the real one: a driver nobody drives is the same failure mode as an armed probe nobody fires, and this device already owns one of those.

questions.a: NAMING, AND IT TOOK TWO PASSES — THE SECOND ONE AKIEN'S. First pass: 'driver' is already a node class (operational-driver) meaning a standing declarative loop that introduces NO new code — the exact inverse of this node on the load-bearing axis — so naming the ticket a driver would have taught every future reader the wrong CLASS before they opened it. Cast instead as `the-shim-builds-a-piece`. Akien, 2026-08-17, on reading it: "it sounds like the shim itself is building instead of just interacting with aider?" HE IS RIGHT, AND IT IS THE SAME DEFECT ONE AXIS OVER: having rejected a name that taught the wrong class, CC picked one that taught the wrong ACTOR. The shim holds aider, hands it a brief, and fences its calls; AIDER builds. Renamed `aider-builds-a-piece` — the subject is the thing that actually does the work, the shim is what it is held behind, and 'a piece' stays because it is decompose's own unit. AND THEN A THIRD PASS, ALSO HIS, ON A DIFFERENT QUESTION ENTIRELY: CC left the dead name standing in the sorted berth (sorted-20260817T102630-a049c8d5e854.json) on the habit that a berth is a record of truth and may not be edited to agree. Akien, 2026-08-17: "record of truth is not a goodness later on when it confuses you. fix it." RULED — the berth is corrected in place, both occurrences, with the dead spelling surviving only inside the correction note that explains it and never as a live id. The reason the habit was wrong here: a record of truth earns its immutability by being EVIDENCE, and a stale id is not evidence of anything — it is a live-looking pointer to a file that does not exist, which costs the next reader a lookup to discover it is dead. What the correction preserves is the actual evidence (CC named it wrong twice in one cast); what it removes is the trap.

THE `builder` DEVICE IS PRIOR ART AND NOT A COLLISION. It owns the seven pre-build machines, states outright that there is no builder process, and its horizon reads 'when the builder becomes a process'. Its falsifier clause (5) reds a non-pre-build machine berthing there, so this berths in aider_shim instead. When builder becomes a process, this becomes one of its HANDS rather than a device of its own.

THE VENV IS AN INTERPRETER BOUNDARY, not a packaging detail: aider is importable only inside the shim's own venv, so the loop is in-process with aider and out-of-process from CC at the same time. A result is therefore serializable data, never a live Coder — which shapes the whole seam and is invisible from outside.

SCOPE NARROWED EXPLICITLY AT CAST: ONE piece, not a loop over the split. Looping needs mid-split failure recovery proved, and it binds a design to an unmeasured assumption about whether decompose's piece size fits a 30B model in one pass. Named so the scope cannot grow silently.

A SECOND WATCH ON THIS DEVICE IS DELIBERATE (and is CC's read, not Akien's ruling). aider_shim_offload_yield asks whether the shimmed ticket passed; aider_shim_edit_survival asks whether the apprentice's own edit survived CC's hand. Those can disagree, and the disagreement is the hollow green. Both wait on the SAME five real tickets, so the second watch costs a probe module and not a second population.

THE TICKET STAMP IS ONE FIELD AND IT IS THE WHOLE DIFFERENCE between a watch that can ever fire and one that cannot: fence.SeenLog.record already takes `ticket`, nothing supplies it, and so the offload probe's population is empty by construction.

PROVED 2026-08-17. THE FALSIFIER IS HALF-MET, AND THE HALF THAT IS NOT MET IS THE FINDING. Its DONE clause has two arms: the offload probe's `shimmed` count moving off 0 (MET — 1 shimmed ticket, 8 verdicts, all pass, the probe's population off zero for the first time in its life), and a piece carried brief -> APPLIED EDIT -> run test result (NOT MET). Two live fires against qwen3-coder:30b on hex, on a 13,932-char brief, both came back as fenced ```python blocks instead of SEARCH/REPLACE, so aider applied nothing: `aider_reported_edited: []`, no file hash moved, 1 allowed ask, 0 reflections. The edit-survival watch's first real reading is therefore `not-applied`, which is exactly the disposition the probe refuses to collapse into `discarded` — 'the apprentice is not producing' and 'the apprentice is being overruled' call for opposite decisions, and this voyage produced the first of the two. Recorded rather than routed around (Law 9): widening the ask cap to buy retries, or changing edit_format, is a bounds question for Akien and not a fix to make unilaterally.

TWO HYPOTHESES KILLED, BOTH BY ONE SHAPE OF ERROR: an expectation that named the ARRANGEMENT and not the code that uses it. (1) 'Model construction reaches no network' was false — aider's ModelInfoManager falls through to a bare requests.get against raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm whenever its 24h JSON cache is cold, and the cache was 19h old when the claim was checked, which is precisely why the first look said no network. The tooth that 'proved' it re-staged the seeding inside its own in-venv script, so it measured the script, not the driver. (2) 'The driver's contribution is ONE kwarg' was false — the stamp was right and the log it reached was in-memory: log_path=None built a SeenLog with record_path=None, so every recorded ask died with the venv process while all 24 teeth passed. A FIXTURE THAT SUPPLIES AN ARGUMENT CAN NEVER FALSIFY THE DEFAULT THAT SUPPLIES NONE — every tooth passed a path, so the default was the one arrangement no fixture could exercise. Found by the first live fire, which is the only thing that could have found it. Both are now scars in driver.py and teeth in the proof; four mutants bite where two did.

THE PROBE'S BERTH PATH WAS GREEN BARE AND RED UNDER NETNS, and the sibling probe's proof carried the same latent defect. The armed check resolved the ticket's spelled berth against the CWD instead of the repo root; this ticket spells its probe path relatively where the sibling's is absolute, so the sibling had been passing for a reason that was luck. Both proofs now call watchme_spec.armed_error and join to the repo root explicitly. THE OTHER LIVE-FIRE SCAR IS AT THE READER: the caller called driver.record on a result drive_brief had already recorded, so the real store carried two rows per drive with byte-identical `at`. The log is append-only and BOTH rows are true, so the collapse belongs to the reader — dispositions() dedups on (ticket, piece_index, at), with a tooth, because `enough` is a count and a store that gained a row by accident would retire the watch having learned four fifths of what it asked for.

THE CHART'S OWN SCORE, MEASURED RATHER THAN JUDGED (/sail step 9). 139 tool calls between the validate berth printing and this close — counted off the session transcript, not estimated: 111 Bash, 16 Edit, 8 Read, 4 Write. Read downward: a good packet is one you barely have to go looking behind, and 139 says this chain was thin. THE NAMED FALSIFICATIONS, second layer, because a score says the packet was thin and never says which field was: (1) SURVEY listed aider's call surfaces but never that ModelInfoManager reaches raw.githubusercontent.com outside litellm entirely — the same structural blindness that made it miss `import litellm` in aider/exceptions.py during the previous voyage, one rung out. (2) SURVEY/HYPOTHESIZE both missed that aider defaults `edit_format` to 'whole' for a model absent from MODEL_SETTINGS, which is the setting the entire drive turns on. (3) HYPOTHESIZE asserted the driver's contribution was one kwarg; the kwarg was right and its default sink was memory, so the hypothesis was true about the line and false about the behaviour. Each of the three is a finding about the CHART LEG that authored the claim, not about the builder's attention — and all three share one shape: a claim read off a call site rather than off a run. Nothing counts these calls and nothing delivers this finding; it is a hand's act today (ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart).

workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(aider_shim_edit_survival) -> [PROVED]

watchme.trigger: each driven piece reaches a disposition — the driver's own result write is the event that already fires, and the comparison is read at the ticket's PROVED crossing. No poll: the driver records the hunks it applied, and the crossing that already happens is what closes the pair.
watchme.enough: five driven pieces with survival recorded — the same five the offload probe waits for, deliberately, so the two watches answer their different questions over ONE population rather than each demanding its own five real tickets
watchme.carrier: per driven piece: the edit as the apprentice applied it, versus the same files as they stand at the ticket's PROVED commit, dispositioned survived | rewritten | discarded. THIS IS THE QUESTION THE OFFLOAD PROBE CANNOT ANSWER: a ticket can pass its physics green while every line the apprentice wrote was thrown away and rewritten by CC — the offload buying nothing while reporting success. A green that was earned by the supervisor rather than the apprentice is a hollow green (Law 8), and nothing today would say so.
watchme.nexus: the hypothesize tree — the same nexus aider_shim_offload_yield deposits to, so the pair (did it pass / did the apprentice's work survive) lands beside the expectation it tests
watchme.consumer: Akien at triage — offload-more vs pull-back is his call, and this is the column that tells him whether a green was earned by the apprentice or by the hand cleaning up after it
